catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class fits a persistent PoseStamped velocity setpoint publication whose only receipt is transmission. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires a duration plus distance, heading and stopped outputs that the upstream controller and this ROS surface do not provide.

No catalogue class fits a sensor_msgs/JointState observation with name, position, velocity and effort arrays. cap.sensing.imu.v1 is the only inertial catalogue class and does not describe joint state.

cap.sensing.imu.v1 binds resource kind sensor.imu, but this configuration-only RosDriver serves one world.sim resource and cannot declare a second sensor resource. The extension also preserves the raw header stamp and frame_id alongside the vectors.

notes:
BLOCKED, not passed. Last gate run: G1 pass Layout and isolation; G2 pass Lock; G3 pass Strict resolve; G4 pass Provenance; G5 pass Reference; G6 fail Behaviour with G6.ESTOP_FAILED: mhs.safety.estop: status failed, MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED: the device reports that its safe state was not reached; the latch stays engaged; retrying in the background (estop 'engaged', expected engaged or software_only); G7 pass Native surface; G8 pass Protocol and surface; G9 skip Repository tests (not run: fix the failing gates first).

Concrete blocker: the pinned upstream exposes no acknowledged stop, pause or reset service or action for its effectful control surface. The three policy controllers only create subscriptions, publishers and a timer; none creates a service server, action server or stop call (robot_controller/robot_controller/load_dreamwaq_policy.py:168-182, load_him_policy.py:200-211, load_wtw_policy.py:103-113). The only shutdown path is rclpy.shutdown() in main (load_dreamwaq_policy.py:281-282, load_him_policy.py:343-345, load_wtw_policy.py:202-204), which the ROS helper documentation does not accept as an acknowledged stop binding. The Gazebo world loads libgazebo_ros_init.so with namespace / (robot_gazebo/worlds/go1_world.world:1122-1126), but the clone does not name or type that plugin's pause/resume services, so a RosDriver source_ref cannot cite the exact endpoint and type at the pinned commit.

Why this is not worked around: a zero-velocity publication, a zero-torque publication or node shutdown is transmission only and is not an acknowledged stop; declaring one as a safe-state action would claim a protection the SDK does not provide. The software latch does engage and refuses further publications (repository test test_an_unconfirmed_estop_still_latches_publications), but the bridge reports bridge_safe_state false and the e-stop receipt is failed SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED, so G6.ESTOP_FAILED is the honest result. A driver that exposes only the IMU/joint-state observations would pass the software-only latch but would drop the primary velocity control, which this task forbids.

The package otherwise resolves and exercises cleanly on the fake: G1-G5, G7 and G8 pass; the nine repository cases (velocity wire fields, joint-state and IMU observations, silent/wrong-id/malformed/failed replies, operator_required refusal, and the latched e-stop) pass. The fake is an analytic ROS-free F0 stand-in with placeholder sensor values, not a recording or a Gazebo run. No hardware backend, ROS graph, Gazebo server, policy checkpoint, network access or hardware run was used or is claimed; driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null. If the upstream later adds an acknowledged ROS stop service/action with a pinned source line, the blocker can be replaced by that binding and the gate re-run.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the three policy controllers create only subscriptions (/robot_velocity_command PoseStamped, /imu_plugin/out Imu, /joint_states JointState), effort and /policy publishers and a timer (load_dreamwaq_policy.py:168-182, load_wtw_policy.py:103-113), and no file of the clone serves or names a ROS service, action, pause or reset endpoint; the Gazebo world loads libgazebo_ros_init with namespace / (go1_world.world:1122-1126) but nothing in the clone names or types its services, so no stop can be bound with a source line, and a zero-velocity publication is transmission only. The stock e-stop therefore fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED with the latch held, which is the honest outcome. The bindings and ROS 2 types, the operator_required velocity bounds with an example overlay, the ROS 2 stamp fields (sec/nanosec) of the fake and the R0 simulated scope were checked. One imprecision remains for the next author: the Walk-These-Ways fact cites load_wtw_policy.py:175-183 for the 0.25 action scale and 0.5 hip reduction, which are set on lines 53-54 (the range shows only self.action_scale and self.hip_scale_reduction). The reviewer changed no authored file; the gate re-run rewrote check-report.json with the same findings (stable digest sha256:ee0a6821956f39b5b0007747d5e92d4a647c7959839a759e25ceaffa954f571f; RESULT.json records the superseded run's report_digest sha256:851cad67...). For the human reviewer: Simulated Go1 in free-running Gazebo: the software latch only stops this driver's publications; a running policy controller keeps applying its last velocity setpoint and Gazebo keeps stepping, and DreamWaQ starts with a 0.15 forward command before anything is published (load_dreamwaq_policy.py:167). The UI publishes /robot_velocity_command only on button or joystick events and no launch starts it (robot_UI/robot_UI/UI_controller.py:19, 46, 56). A possible unblocking route is the pause_physics/unpause_physics/reset services that gazebo_ros_init (outside the clone) serves in the root namespace, which no file of the clone names; binding them needs a citation the gate accepts. The README's Real Robot Integration is 'Coming soon', so no hardware path exists.
